title: Compose runs fail when registry logins are set: DOCKER_CONFIG hides CLI plugins
description: With registry credentials configured, ComposeExecutionService sets DOCKER_CONFIG to a temp dir containing only config.json {auths}. The docker CLI then looks for plugins only in $DOCKER_CONFIG/cli-plugins (plus system dirs), so on Docker Desktop (plugins symlinked in ~/.docker/cli-plugins) 'docker compose' is not found and every run fails with "unknown shorthand flag: 'p' in -p" (surfaced as invalid compose file). Buildx fallback is affected the same way. Repro: DOCKER_CONFIG=$(mktemp -d) docker compose -p x version.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The temp config.json written for registry auths also sets cliPluginsExtraDirs to the plugin dirs of the original config (${DOCKER_CONFIG:-~/.docker}/cli-plugins) plus known system dirs that exist (Docker Desktop /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/cli-plugins, /usr/local/lib/docker/cli-plugins, /usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins, /usr/lib/docker/cli-plugins, Homebrew lib/docker/cli-plugins); existing cliPluginsExtraDirs from the original config.json are preserved if readable. 2. No auths -> environment untouched (unchanged). 3. Unit test in ComposeExecutionServiceTest asserts config.json contains auths and cliPluginsExtraDirs. 4. Real-Docker test (skipped without docker/compose) runs 'docker compose version' through ComposeExecutionService with a fake registry auth and succeeds. 5. Secrets still never logged; temp dir still 0700/0600 and deleted in finally. 6. CLAUDE.md code map entry for RegistryAuthSource/ComposeExecutionService mentions cliPluginsExtraDirs.
close_reason: Temp DOCKER_CONFIG now sets cliPluginsExtraDirs; pushed to dev

title: Create, edit and deploy Compose stacks (editor, wizard, env vars, GitHub repos with polling)
description:
Goal: ADMIN and OPERATOR can create new Compose stacks on an environment, edit them (raw YAML editor or form wizard for services, ports, env vars, volumes, networks, restart policy), deploy/stop/delete them with live output, see version history and roll back. Stacks can also come from a (private) GitHub repo/org, with manual 'Pull & redeploy' and optional polling auto-update. VIEWER is read-only.

Decisions (scope check 2026-10-23):
- Stack files live on a backend volume under configurable `shipir.stacks.base-dir` (e.g. /data/stacks), one dir per <host-id>/<stack-name>. DB (stack_versions) is the source of truth; files are (re)written on deploy. All paths go through PathValidationUtil. Resolves the HANDOFF open decision for stack dirs (config editor base dir stays open).
- Compose runs as `docker compose` subprocess (ProcessBuilder, arg list) with DOCKER_HOST for TCP hosts; TLS material written to a short-lived 0700 temp dir and deleted afterwards.
- GitHub auth: ADMIN-managed named Git credentials (username + PAT, works for orgs), AES-GCM encrypted via SecretCipher, never logged or returned.
- Git scope: create stack from repo (URL, branch, compose path, credential), manual Pull & redeploy, plus polling auto-update (per-stack interval). No GitHub webhooks.
- Roles: ADMIN+OPERATOR write stacks; Git credentials ADMIN-only; per-stack permissions later (permission epic).
- Env vars stored per StackVersion encrypted (may hold secrets), written as .env next to compose file.
- Assumption: Git access via JGit (no git binary, token via CredentialsProvider, never in URL).

Out of scope: adopting/editing stacks Shipir did not create (shown read-only as today), GitHub webhooks, GitHub App/OAuth, per-stack permissions, config editor, exec terminal/log streaming.
acceptance_criteria:
- ADMIN/OPERATOR create a stack via YAML editor or wizard, with env vars, and deploy it to LOCAL or TCP environment; output streams live
- Edit + redeploy creates a new version; rollback redeploys an older version
- Stop/delete work; VIEWER sees stacks but no write actions
- ADMIN stores a GitHub PAT; a stack from a private repo deploys, Pull & redeploy picks up new commits, polling auto-redeploys when enabled
- Secrets (PAT, env values, TLS) never appear in logs, API responses or audit details

title: App shell with user settings, notifications, retention rules and audit log
description:

Every role gets in-app notifications when an environment goes DOWN or comes back UP. ADMINs get a Settings section with notification webhooks, retention rules and the audit log.

Scope in:
- Frontend app shell: sidebar + top bar user menu (Settings, Sign out), routes /, /environments/:id, /notifications, /account, /settings/{notifications,retention,audit-log}.
- Personal user settings (/account, all roles): account info (username, role, read-only), change password (existing POST /api/auth/password), own notification preferences.
- Notifications: background host health check (HostHealthCheckScheduler) publishes HostStatusChangedEvent on DOWN/UP transitions; new notification/ module fans out per-user in-app notifications (respecting each user's preferences); notifications tab with unread badge, mark read / mark all read.
- Webhooks (ADMIN): outgoing HTTP POST with a generic JSON payload per enabled event type, test send. Webhook URLs are secrets (tokens in URL): encrypted at rest with SecretCipher, never returned in full or logged.
- Audit log: brings the planned audit module (build order step 7) forward: V8 create_audit_log, @Auditable + AuditAspect (AOP), ADMIN-only paged read API and page.
- Retention rules (ADMIN): days to keep audit log entries and notifications, daily scheduled purge.

Scope out: email/SMTP delivery (password reset sender stays NoOp), Shipir app/backend log viewer, container log streaming, profile fields (display name, email), fine-grained permissions, provider-specific webhook formats (Discord/Slack payloads), user management.

Decisions (scope check 2026-10-23, user):
- 'Logs' = audit log (who did what), not app logs.
- Notifications v1 = in-app for host status changes + outgoing webhooks. No email.
- User settings page = account info + change password + notification preferences.
- Sidebar Settings section and its APIs are ADMIN only; notifications tab and /account are for every role.

Design decisions (planning):
- New packages notification/ and retention/ (added to the CLAUDE.md architecture tree). host/ publishes HostStatusChangedEvent as a Spring ApplicationEvent and knows nothing about notification/. retention/ uses audit/ and notification/ repositories.
- Health check keeps the last known status in memory; the first check after startup only sets the baseline (no notification), so a restart does not spam notifications.
- Notifications are stored per user (fan-out at creation), user FK ON DELETE CASCADE, host FK ON DELETE SET NULL with a host name snapshot.
- Audit entries keep a username snapshot; user_id nullable ON DELETE SET NULL so history survives (failed logins have no user id). Details never contain secrets.
- Migrations: V8__create_audit_log, V9__create_notifications, V10__create_notification_webhooks, V11__create_retention_settings (HANDOFF planned V8+ for config_files/permissions shift accordingly; update HANDOFF.md 'Planned migrations' at finish).
acceptance_criteria:
- Signed-in users see a left sidebar (Environments, Notifications; Settings only for ADMIN) and a top bar user menu with Settings and Sign out.
- Any user can change their password and notification preferences under the user menu > Settings.
- When an environment goes DOWN or back UP, users who opted in get an in-app notification; the sidebar shows the unread count; notifications can be marked read.
- ADMIN can configure webhooks that receive host status events, send a test, and never sees the stored URL in full again.
- ADMIN can view a paged, filterable audit log of logins, password changes and environment/settings changes.
- ADMIN can set retention days for audit log and notifications; older entries are purged daily.
- OPERATOR/VIEWER get 403 on all settings/audit/webhook endpoints and do not see the Settings section.

title: Add password reset code domain: entity, repository, service and delivery port
description:

- auth/PasswordResetProperties.java: shipir.password-reset.code-ttl (default 5m) and max-attempts (default 5).
- auth/PasswordResetService.java:
  - requestReset(username): unknown user -> no-op, no exception, no difference visible to the caller. Known user -> invalidate the user's open codes, generate a 6-digit code (SecureRandom, zero-padded), store SHA-256 hex, expires_at = now + ttl, call the sender with the plain code.
  - confirmReset(username, code, newPassword): find the latest open code (not used, not expired, failed_attempts < max). Compare hashes in constant time (MessageDigest.isEqual). On a mismatch, increment failed_attempts. Unknown user, wrong, expired, used or exhausted all throw the same package-private InvalidResetCodeException. Validate newPassword with PasswordPolicy (same violations/exception style as UserService.changePassword). On success: new Argon2 hash and passwordChangedAt via User.changePasswordHash, mark the code used (used_at), all in one transaction.
- Inject java.time.Clock so expiry is testable (add a Clock bean if none exists).
Reuse PasswordPolicy and PasswordEncoder. No controller in this task.

title: Self-service password reset with one-time code
description:
Goal: a user who forgot their password (any role) can reset it from the login page with a one-time code that is valid for 5 minutes.

Scope in:
- 'Forgot password?' on the login page. The user enters their username, then the code and a new password.
- Backend: the code is stored only as a SHA-256 hash in a new table. It is handed to a delivery port PasswordResetCodeSender. For now the port has a no-op adapter, and a mailing service implements it later.
- Frontend flow with Vitest and Playwright tests.

Scope out:
- Mailing service and users.email column (later epic). Until then, a real user can't receive the code. Only tests can read it, through the port.
- Invalidating the user's other active sessions after a reset (needs a session registry; follow-up).
- Rate limiting reset requests per IP or username beyond 'new request invalidates the old code'.
- Admin-initiated resets and user management.
- Cleanup job for expired rows.

Decisions (scope check 2026-10-23):
- Self-service by username. The request endpoint always answers 202, so accounts can't be enumerated.
- The code is never stored in plain text (CLAUDE.md security rule): SHA-256 hash only, and the code is never logged.
- Code: 6 digits from SecureRandom, single use, TTL 5 min. It is burned after 5 wrong attempts, and a new request invalidates earlier codes.
- Confirm uses the same 400 INVALID_RESET_CODE for unknown user, wrong, expired, used or exhausted codes.
- The new password goes through PasswordPolicy. A successful reset sets passwordChangedAt, which also completes the PASSWORD setup step.
- Migration numbering: this takes V7. HANDOFF's planned V5-V7 names for config_files/permissions/audit_log shift accordingly.
acceptance_criteria:
- From the login page, a user can request a reset code for their username, enter the code plus a new password that meets the policy, and then sign in with the new password.
- Unknown usernames give the same response as known ones.
- The code works once, expires after 5 minutes, and stops working after 5 wrong attempts.
- No reset code is stored or logged in plain text.

title: Docker environments: Portainer-style overview and environment step in first-start setup
description:
Goal: after login every user sees an overview of all Docker environments (like the Portainer home screen): status, endpoint, Docker version, CPU/RAM, container counts (running/stopped/healthy/unhealthy), images, volumes. The first-start setup gets a required second step where the admin adds the first environment.

Scope IN:
- Connection types LOCAL (Unix socket mounted into the backend) and TCP with TLS client certificates.
- host/ backend: DockerHost entity, CRUD API, connection test. docker/ backend: docker-java behind our own interfaces, per-host client management, system info.
- Live overview: the backend queries every environment per request (short timeout, failure = DOWN for that environment only). The frontend refetches on an interval. No snapshot table.
- First-start setup: password step (exists), then a required environment step (Local or TCP+TLS, with connection test). setupRequired stays true for the ADMIN until at least one environment exists.
- Roles: only ADMIN creates/renames/deletes environments and the connection test. All roles see the overview (all environments; fine-grained permissions come later).
- Clicking an environment opens a placeholder environment page.
- Deployment: socket mount + SHIPIR_ENCRYPTION_KEY in docker-compose.yml / .env.example / README.

Scope OUT: per-environment dashboard (containers/images/volumes lists), stack count per environment (needs compose/ repositories), snapshots/history, plain TCP without TLS, agent/tunnel connections, fine-grained permissions, audit log entries.

Decisions (scope check 2026-10-23):
- TLS material (CA, client cert, client key) is uploaded as PEM in the UI, encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a master key from SHIPIR_ENCRYPTION_KEY (property shipir.encryption-key, base64, 32 bytes) and stored in the DB (migration V6). It is never logged and never returned by the API.
- The key is optional while only LOCAL environments exist. Creating a TCP environment without a key fails with a clear error, and startup fails if TCP environments exist but the key is missing or invalid.
- Setup offers both Local and TCP+TLS, reusing the same form as Add environment.
- Live per-request stats instead of Portainer's periodic snapshots.
- Note: HANDOFF.md planned V5__create_config_files; V5 is already used (password_changed_at), so later planned migrations shift by one more.

API contract (shared by backend and frontend children):
- GET /api/hosts -> [{id, name, connectionType: LOCAL|TCP, host, port, tls: boolean, createdAt}] (all roles)
- POST /api/hosts {name, connectionType, host?, port?, tlsCaPem?, tlsCertPem?, tlsKeyPem?} -> 201 host (ADMIN). The connection is tested before saving; 422 CONNECTION_FAILED on failure.
- POST /api/hosts/connection-test (same body, name optional) -> 200 {ok, dockerVersion?, errorCode?, message?} (ADMIN)
- PATCH /api/hosts/{id} {name} -> 200 host (ADMIN); DELETE /api/hosts/{id} -> 204 (ADMIN)
- GET /api/hosts/overview -> [{id, name, connectionType, endpoint, status: UP|DOWN, error?, dockerVersion, cpus, memoryBytes, containers: {running, stopped, healthy, unhealthy}, images, volumes}] (all roles)
- GET /api/auth/me additionally returns setupStep: PASSWORD | ENVIRONMENT | null
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh install: admin logs in, sets a password, is then required to add a Docker environment (Local or TCP+TLS, connection checked) before reaching the app.
- After setup every user sees an environment overview with status and live stats per environment, similar to the Portainer home screen; an unreachable environment shows as down without breaking the page.
- ADMIN can add, rename and delete environments from the overview; OPERATOR/VIEWER only see them.
- TLS keys/certs are stored encrypted and never appear in API responses or logs.
- The hosting docker-compose.yml documents and supports the socket mount and the encryption key.
close_reason: Docker environments: LOCAL + TCP/TLS hosts, live overview, setup environment step, admin management

title: Restructure CI/CD: tests gate prd image builds, path-filtered tests on dev
description:
Goal: save GitHub runner minutes while keeping test coverage. Today .github/workflows/images.yml builds both images on every PR and on pushes to dev/prd/v* tags, and no tests run in CI at all.

- Push to dev and pull requests: only the tests of the area that changed (backend/ -> backend tests, frontend/ -> frontend tests). No e2e, no image build.
- Push of a v* tag: no tests, no build; the already-built prd image (sha-<commit>) is re-tagged with the semver tags (1.2.3, 1.2, 1; major skipped for v0.x).

- v* tags re-tag the tested prd image via docker buildx imagetools create instead of rebuilding.
- PRs behave like dev pushes (path-filtered tests).
- The :dev image tag is dropped (no images from dev anymore).
- Structure: one reusable test workflow (workflow_call) used by the dev/PR workflow and the prd workflow, so test steps are defined once.

Out of scope: deployments, branch protection settings, caching beyond standard setup-java/pnpm/gha caches, ArchUnit.
Release flow stays as in CLAUDE.md (git push origin dev:prd, then tag v*).,
acceptance_criteria:
- Pushing to dev or opening a PR runs only the tests for changed areas (backend and/or frontend), no e2e, no image build
- Pushing to prd runs all tests + e2e, and images are pushed to ghcr.io only when they pass
- Pushing a v* tag publishes semver tags pointing at the same image digest as the prd sha image, without rebuilding
- images.yml no longer exists; README and CLAUDE.md describe the new pipeline

title: Login page with first-start setup (forced password change)
description:
Goal: Shipir is protected by a login. On first start an initial admin exists; after the first login that admin must set a secure password on a setup screen before anything else is usable. Later logins show only the login page.

Scope in: Spring Security with server-side session, initial admin seeding, login/logout/me endpoints, password change with policy, setup gate (backend + frontend), login page, setup page.
Scope out: user management (create/delete users, roles UI), fine-grained permissions, rate limiting / lockout for login attempts, password reset, WebSocket auth (no STOMP endpoints yet), audit logging of logins (comes with audit/).

Decisions (scope check, 2026-10-23):
- Auth: server-side Spring Security session (HttpOnly cookie, cookie-based CSRF for the SPA), not JWT. Recorded in HANDOFF.md.
- Initial admin: if the users table is empty at startup, create user 'admin' (role ADMIN) with the password from SHIPIR_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD (property shipir.initial-admin.password). BCrypt-hashed, never logged. Startup fails with a clear message if users is empty and the variable is missing. No well-known default password.
- Setup flag: new column users.password_changed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL (migration V5). NULL = setup required (the user's 'first_login empty -> setup screen' idea, named for what it records).
- Password policy: 15-128 characters, at least one uppercase letter, lowercase letter, digit and symbol (non-alphanumeric); must differ from the current password and from the username.

API contract (shared by backend and frontend children):
- GET  /api/auth/me -> 200 {username, role, setupRequired} | 401
- POST /api/auth/login {username, password} -> 200 {username, role, setupRequired} | 401 generic "invalid credentials" (no hint whether the user exists)
- POST /api/auth/logout -> 204, session invalidated
- POST /api/auth/password {currentPassword, newPassword} -> 204 | 400 {code:"PASSWORD_POLICY", violations:[...]} | 400 {code:"INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD"}
- While setupRequired: every other /api/** -> 403 {code:"SETUP_REQUIRED"}
- CSRF: cookie XSRF-TOKEN (readable by JS), sent back as header X-XSRF-TOKEN on every non-GET request, including login.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh install: open Shipir, see a login page, sign in as admin with SHIPIR_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD, land on the setup screen, cannot reach anything else until a password matching the policy is set.
- After setup, the app is reachable; logout and the next login go straight to the app with no setup screen.
- Unauthenticated API calls get 401; wrong credentials give a generic error.
close_reason: Login with session auth and forced first-start password change, backend + frontend

Read-only: the skill only uses gh run list/view/watch and gh auth status.

title: Enforce at most one LOCAL docker host with a partial unique index
description: HostService (shipr-406.5) checks 'only one LOCAL environment' in the service only. Two concurrent POST /api/hosts with connectionType LOCAL can both pass the check and both be saved, since V6 has no DB constraint for it. Add a migration with a partial unique index on docker_hosts ((connection_type)) WHERE connection_type = 'LOCAL', and map its violation to 409 LOCAL_HOST_EXISTS in HostService (today any DataIntegrityViolationException on save maps to HOST_NAME_TAKEN).
acceptance_criteria: New migration adds the partial unique index; SchemaMigrationTest rejects a second LOCAL row; HostService maps the index violation to 409 LOCAL_HOST_EXISTS and a name collision still to 409 HOST_NAME_TAKEN; ./backend/mvnw -f backend/pom.xml verify passes.
